_comment: SmartCuff GUI update manifest. Fetched by the installed GUI over plain
public HTTPS -- there is deliberately NO credential in the client. See
README.md for why an embedded token was rejected.
This file is the ONLY thing the updater needs to read. Keep it small and
keep it valid JSON: a malformed manifest must fail soft in the client, but
there is no reason to rely on that.
The installer is a GitHub Release asset rather than a repository blob.
Keep installer_url version-specific: an existing manifest must always
resolve to the exact immutable bytes whose size and SHA-256 it declares.
notes:
Smart Cuff v3.1.356 (Default) with firmware rev27v-followup-339 (unchanged from v3.1.355).

Tab switching is about three times faster. Each workspace page keeps its own colour theme, and a switch re-themes only the shared header, event log, plot and notification areas instead of the whole window, which used to pause the interface for a quarter of a second or more per switch, including during runs. Pages look the same as before.

System ID no longer stops on the probe where the valve opens: when quiet readings around a probe rule out pulses, a fast smooth fall may depart from the fitted curve by up to 2 % of how far it falls. System ID learns how far this cuff overshoots each inflation, separately for top-ups and full inflations in each pressure range, and stops the pump earlier on later inflations so the pressure no longer jumps past its targets. When a band reaches the high-pressure time limit before its next probe, System ID now vents, recovers and continues that band (at most twice) instead of stopping; the limit itself is unchanged. On Device D (wrist cuff on syringe) a compare-only System ID now runs through all three bands; its quality checks still decide whether a result is acceptable.
_channel_note: stable is the only channel today. If a test channel is ever added, publish
a second manifest (version-beta.json) rather than adding branching logic to
the client -- the client stays a dumb fetch-and-compare.
